scope: Read-only review of frozen extension background, extraction grouping, UI and version-1 state compatibility. Native archive parser/path safety and personal Chrome/live downloads were out of scope.

summary.result: No confirmed P0/P1 issue in reviewed scope. One recoverability/UI-state issue is confirmed for removing a constituent item from a failed multi-volume extraction group.

findings.title: Removing a part from a failed volume group leaves an unrecoverable retry group
findings.trigger: A split archive extraction has failed. The user removes one completed queue item belonging to the failed group, then selects another remaining part and presses Retry Extraction.
findings.expected: The UI should prevent removal while the group still references the item, or update/detach the group so its retry state accurately reflects the remaining source set.
findings.actual: The remove guard blocks only groups in queued/extracting states. For a failed group, removal deletes the QueueItem but leaves its ID in group.itemIds; it only changes groups whose status is waiting. Retry resets the group to waiting and syncExtractions calls extractionPaths for every saved ID. The missing item makes extractionPaths throw source_unavailable, so the group returns to failed and cannot be repaired from the remaining UI records.
findings.impact: The remaining archive parts keep displaying a retry action that can never succeed; there is no command/UI to edit the group membership or re-associate the deleted part. The user must retain or recreate queue records through a new batch to recover cleanly.
minimalRepro: Add a complete two-part set (for example book.part1.rar and book.part2.rar) with auto-extraction enabled.
Cause extraction to fail so the group status is failed.
Remove one completed part using its row remove action; removal is allowed because the group is failed.
Open the other part and choose Retry Extraction; the group still requests the removed item ID and resolves to source_unavailable.
findings.evidence: Frozen snapshot code: remove() rejects only queued/extracting groups at engine.ts:540-545, deletes the item at :547, and only marks waiting groups failed at :548-552. The UI exposes remove for every non-active row at main.ts:210. retry-extraction resets failed groups to waiting at engine.ts:690-695; extractionPaths rejects absent IDs at :235-238 and syncExtractions maps that failure back to failed at :335-344.

verifiedBehavior: Version 1 persisted state is spread-forward with settings defaults and item event normalization; optional extractions remains absent safely for older state.
Ordinary add without extraction does not call the native helper; enabling extraction intentionally requires helper ping/secret storage before adding the batch.
Extraction groups wait for every tracked item to complete; unresolved groups use Chrome download filenames when all selected items complete.

The saved native job ID is written before native status/start side effects and reused on subsequent synchronization; startup and alarms reconcile extraction state even while the download queue is paused.
Batch password is sent to native store-secret and only secret IDs are kept in extension queue state; UI clears the password field after a successful add.

performed: Verified manifest SHA-256 and every listed snapshot file byte count/SHA-256 against the manifest.
Read-only source tracing of add, extraction resolution/status sync, pause, retry, remove, clear-complete, startup/alarm handling, volume grouping, UI actions and state loading.
notPerformed: No tests were run in this review; the parent task reported the existing 107-test suite passing and is adding focused deferred-ID/busy/failed-retry tests.
No personal Chrome profile, registry, live downloads or native extraction operation was accessed.

unknowns: This report is based on the pinned snapshot only. Behavior in files omitted from its manifest and any later working-tree edits was not used to reach findings.
Native compression/parser and path-safety behavior was not independently audited, per task scope.
